observations.finding: Treated fields less confluent than DMSO control (DMSO: dense confluent monolayer >200 cells/field; 0.1uM: 89 cells measured sparse single cells, 3.0uM: 211 cells measured loose clusters).
F-actin (red) markedly increased vs DMSO: thick bright peripheral band with spiky/filopodial protrusions, texture more heterogeneous. DMSO red is faint thin cell border.
Actin intensity and variation increased: act_mean z +23.7/ +19.2, act_std z +15.2/ +10.9, act_glcm_contrast z +16.8/ +10.0 vs DMSO.
Green tubulin relatively dimmer vs red, especially at 3.0uM diffuse perinuclear green reduced.
Actin dominates tubulin (red >> green, yellow where overlap) vs DMSO balanced green/red.
Tubulin mean decreased at 3.0uM (tub_mean z -9.1) and tub texture more heterogeneous at 0.1uM (tub_glcm_contrast z +7.3).

DNA (blue DAPI) nuclei irregular, lobed, eccentric: 0.1uM ~1-2 nuclei/cell often bilobed, 3.0uM extensive multinucleation/micronucleation with clusters of 5-20 small blue fragments per cell and scattered enlarged cells.

Nuclear shape metrics reflect irregularity: nuc_solidity z -24.2 / -20.3, nuc_form_factor z -12.3 / -12.0, nuc_eccentricity z +9.0 at 0.1uM, and frac_large_nucleus z +11.0 at 3.0uM vs DMSO oval round nuclei.

notable_cells.why: Example enlarged cell with >10 micronuclei (small blue dots) and bright red actin rim, typical of 3.0uM fields
Example bilobed/irregular nucleus with bright peripheral actin at 0.1uM

candidate_mechanisms.why: Failed cytokinesis/polyploidy phenotype: solidity/form_factor loss, eccentricity increase, large nuclei and dose-dependent micronucleation/multinucleation plus actin remodeling with increased act_tub_ratio, matches classic Aurora B inhibition. 3.0uM strongly characteristic.

report.uncertainty: No separate grayscale channels; tubulin vs actin read from green/red/yellow in composite. Mitotic spindle detail not resolvable.

data.note:
Specimen s_66b994c89e = nocodazole confirmed as Microtubule destabilizers. PubChem CID 4122 (IUPAC methyl N-[6-(thiophene-2-carbonyl)-1H-benzimidazol-2-yl]carbamate, C14H11N3O3S) matches BBBC021 structure; ChEMBL CHEMBL9514 has no curated mechanism entry but literature consensus is tubulin polymerization inhibitor binding colchicine site class (e.g. colchicine-site destabilizers PMID:28640209).

Phenotype we measured matches destabilizer: dose-dependent tub_mean loss (rho -1.0, z -9.1 at 3µM to +9.1 at 0.03µM) with reciprocal act_tub_ratio gain (rho +1.0, z +43 at 3µM), irregular lobed/multinucleated nuclei (nuc_solidity z -30, nuc_form_factor z -24, frac_large_nucleus z +17 at 1µM) and dim diffuse tubulin vs bright actin rim. NSC 2/2 split destabilizer vs stabilizer but summed similarity and 9/10 k-neighbors (vincristine/demecolcine, similarities 0.67-0.80) favor destabilizer - consistent with nocodazole's known depolymerization leading to failed cytokinesis/polyploidy. Correct call.

reflection.text:
Reflection - nocodazole (CID 4122) unblinded as Microtubule destabilizers - verdict correct, protocol and Scientist concur (p=0.70).

What got it right:

1. High-dose bracketing was decisive. Acquiring well w_99b0bb31f5 dose 7 3uM rep1 first (e2) gave extreme act_tub_ratio z=+43.4 and act_mean z=+19.2 with nuc_solidity z=-20.3/n -24.2. This established actin dominance via tubulin loss, not actin gain alone. The follow-up well w_0fd9e97372 dose 6 1uM rep1 (e12) confirmed it at 32.3 / -30.4 / -24.2 for act_tub_ratio / nuc_solidity / nuc_form_factor with 188 cells. These two high-dose wells both 1-NN to Microtubule destabilizers with similarities 0.75 and 0.798 in the protocol tally.

2. Monotonic dose-response separated destabilizer vs stabilizer vs Aurora. Over 3 wells/3 doses (0.03-3uM): act_tub_ratio rho=+1.00 p=0 (e8), tub_mean rho=-1.00 p=0 (e10), nuc_area rho=+1.00 p=0 (e11). Review correctly summarized tub_mean ~+9.1 to -9.1 and act_tub_ratio +5.2 to +43.4. Stabilizers would not explain dose-dependent tub_mean loss; that was the key contradicting evidence for e14 Microtubule stabilizers hypothesis (0.15) listed as e8/e10. Aurora hypothesis (e14 0.10) was correctly downweighted because frac_mitotic_like was constant across acquired wells (e9) and atlas did not support it.

3. Atlas consensus beyond the tied NSC vote. Initial compare (e5) over 2 wells: NSC 1/2 destabilizers but k-neighbour 10/10 destabilizers. Final compare (e13) over 4 wells: NSC 2/4 destabilizers, k-neighbour 9/10 destabilizers 1/10 stabilizers. Protocol tally was 2-2 but summed similarity 1.548 vs 1.311 favored destabilizers, matching Scientist key evidence e5,e13. This was used in rationale for submit_conclusion (e15): tied vote but k=10 and monotonic tub loss favor depolymerization.

What misled / what was missed:

- describe_phenotype e4 (Microscopist on 4 fields: density lower vs DMSO, 8 observations, candidates: Aurora kinase inhibitors) was the main misleading cue. It was driven by the very strong nuclear irregularity signal present at all doses: nuc_solidity z=-24.2 at 0.1uM (e3), -21.6 at 0.03uM (e6) with tub_glcm_contrast z=+22.4, -20.3 at 3uM (e2), -30.4 at 1uM (e12). Combined with lower density, this phenocopies Aurora polyploidy/multinucleation. I kept Aurora at 0.10 in update_hypotheses (e14) with e4 as sole supporting, contradicting e5/e13/e9, which was appropriate but the visual anchor delayed certainty.

- Low-intermediate doses classified as stabilizers in protocol per-well table: w_ded8987f6d 0.03uM similarity 0.618 to stabilizers and w_1db1c2db0e 0.1uM 0.692 to stabilizers. Acquisition of w_1db1c2db0e (e3) at 0.1uM with 89 cells gave act_tub_ratio +20.1 despite low cell count, and e6 at 0.03uM retained tub_glcm_contrast +22.4. These intermediate phenotypes are near-threshold and explain the 2-2 split. The nuc_solidity dose-response e7 rho=+0.50 p=0.67 also failed to show expected dose strengthening, reinforcing that nuclear shape alone is non-specific.

- Actin disruptor hypothesis (e14 0.05, supporting e2/e3) was considered due to high act_mean z +19.2 to +23.7, but correctly contradicted by e10 tub_mean loss and e13 atlas, since actin disruptors would not produce progressive microtubule loss.

Why decisions were made:

- list_available_experiments (e1) showed 8 doses 0.001-3uM with 4 wells budget; strategy to sample high (e2), mid (e3), low-intermediate (e6), then high-intermediate (e12) was to resolve trajectory. The final 1uM acquisition (e12) was explicitly to resolve split NSC vote and succeeded.

- Dose-response tool choices e7-e11 were necessary to distinguish mechanisms sharing nuclear irregularity. act_tub_ratio gain + tub_mean loss + nuc_area gain together point to depolymerization and failed cytokinesis/polyploidy rather than stabilization or Aurora-selective mitotic arrest.

Unblinding checks: lookup_compound e16/e17 confirmed nocodazole CID 4122 CHEMBL9514 identity_check name and BBBC021 structure agree but chembl_mechanisms none curated, so no prior label to bias call. search_literature e18 returned 14 hits for nocodazole destabilizer and e19 0 hits for destabilizer multinucleation actin in MCF-7; no PMID from this run directly supports a specific claim, so no citation is applied.

Lesson: Nuclear irregularity/multinucleation + lower density is sensitive but not specific between Aurora and microtubule destabilizers; tub_mean dose-response directionality and summed similarity/k-neighbour consensus are required to break the tie, and budget exhaustion at 4/4 wells left no affordable tie-breaker beyond decisiveness calibration at 0.70.
